hypotheses.title: Options Forward Price Borrow-Cost Squeeze Anomaly
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Forward price curves (forward_price_20 / close) reflect the net cost of carry and institutional borrowing expectations. Stocks where forward prices trade at an abnormal discount to spot price (forward_price_20 < close) reflect high borrowing demand from short sellers (hard-to-borrow pressure). When short borrow demand normalizes, these equities experience sharp short squeezes and mean reversion. Market-wide ranking ensures complete universe coverage with zero subindustry starvation.
confounders: Persistent hard-to-borrow distress leading to direct equity restructuring or delisting
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if forward discount stocks continue falling without experiencing a short-squeeze rebound.

hypotheses.title: Systematic Market Correlation Decoupling and Intraday VWAP Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Equities with low rolling correlation to SPY (-correlation_last_60_days_spy) provide structural diversification and insulation from market-wide macroeconomic shocks. Combining low market correlation with short-term intraday price-VWAP mean-reversion isolates idiosyncratic outperformance with minimal portfolio market risk.
confounders: Sudden correlation breakdown caused by idiosyncratic operational crisis rather than defensive quality
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if low correlation stocks exhibit negative excess returns during broader market advances.

candidates.expression: 0.60 * group_rank(-correlation_last_60_days_spy, subindustry) - 0.40 * group_rank(ts_decay_linear((close - vwap) / close, 5), subindustry)

hypotheses.title: Quarterly Cash Dividend Yield with Price Delta Rebalancing
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Dividend declarations represent direct, unencumbered cash return to shareholders. Cash dividend yields (actual_dividend_value_qua / close) normalized within subindustries identify disciplined capital-returning firms with strong balance-sheet resilience. Coupling with 5-day price-delta mean reversion maintains turnover in the optimal 12-16% sweet spot.
confounders: Dividend traps where management maintains unsustainable payout ratios from borrowed debt
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if dividend-paying firms suffer valuation multiple contraction compared to capital-reinvesting peers.
